skill.name: deep-search
skill.description: Turn a plain-language web research request into a table with a source URL and read time for each value. Approve a maximum price before a paid search starts.
skill.summary: Build sourced tables from live web research with an upfront price quote.
skill.author: specstream

security_audit.summary: The shell execution and system reconnaissance alerts are false positives, and the documentation URL is a reference. The search request goes to SpecStream before price approval, and paid searches can collect personal contact details in bulk. The skill requires approval of the exact quoted maximum before starting paid work.

remediation.issue: Search terms can leave the workspace before price approval.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the external transfer before compiling and ask users to remove secrets or confidential details. Require separate approval before sending sensitive requests.

remediation.issue: Table searches and exports can collect personal contact details in bulk.
remediation.suggestion: Exclude personal emails and phone numbers by default. Require an explicit opt-in and limit collection and export to the fields and records needed for a stated purpose.

content.user_title: Build Sourced Tables from Live Web Research
content.value_statement: Collecting the same facts from many web pages takes time and makes sources hard to track. Deep Search organizes matches into a table, cites each value, and asks you to approve a maximum price.
actual_capabilities: Turn a plain-language request into a specification with a record type, required conditions, and fields.
Revise conditions or fields before requesting a price.
Show the maximum cost and quote expiration before asking for approval.
Track search progress and retrieve all pages of returned rows.
Show source URLs and read times for returned values and review sources for condition checks.
Export the returned rows to a file.
limitations: The skill requires the SpecStream MCP connector and browser sign-in on first use.
Returned rows do not guarantee complete coverage of the live web.
Adding rows or fields or rechecking a finished table requires a new quote and approval.
The service receives search terms during compilation, before you approve paid work.

use_cases.title: Compare Public Supplier Terms
use_cases.description: Build a table of suppliers with public delivery terms and minimum order quantities.

use_cases.title: Catalog Public Programs
use_cases.description: Collect public grant programs with eligibility rules, deadlines, and links to official sources.

use_cases.title: Find Venues with Published Access Details
use_cases.description: Compare venue capacity and published accessibility features before contacting shortlisted locations.

prompt_templates.title: List Public Venues
prompt_templates.scenario: Request a simple table with two fields.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find public libraries in Tacoma, Washington. Return each library name and street address with source links. Show the maximum price and wait for my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Filter Products by Published Criteria
prompt_templates.scenario: Specify required conditions and comparison fields.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find portable monitors with USB-C power and a published weight under two pounds. Return the model, weight, and power requirements. Quote the search before starting it.

prompt_templates.title: Review Conditions Before Pricing
prompt_templates.scenario: Check the scope of eligibility research before requesting a quote.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a search for open Oregon grants that accept nonprofit applicants. Include the program name, application deadline, and eligibility criteria. Let me review the conditions and fields before requesting a quote.

prompt_templates.title: Verify and Export a Sourced Dataset
prompt_templates.scenario: Review condition checks and export the complete results.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find conference venues in Seattle with published capacity for at least 200 attendees and step-free entry. Return venue name, capacity, and access details. Show the maximum price and wait for approval. After the run finishes, retrieve every page, include sources for condition checks, and export the table.

output_examples.input: Draft a search for libraries in Tacoma, Washington.
output_examples.output: Record type: public library. Required condition: located in Tacoma, Washington. Requested fields: library name and street address. No paid work has started.

output_examples.input: What does a finished public grant search return?
output: One row per returned grant, with columns for program name, application deadline, and eligibility criteria.
A source URL and read time beside each returned value.
Separate condition checks with sources and a file export on request.

best_practices: Specify the record type, required conditions, and fields before requesting a quote.
Review the maximum cost and expiration before authorizing paid work.
Check sources for important values and omit sensitive details from the search request.
anti_patterns: Using a paid table search for a single fact or the text of a known page.
Treating an account balance or earlier approval as consent for a new run.
Treating the first results page as the full result set.

faq.question: What do I need to connect?
faq.answer: Use the configured SpecStream MCP connector. The connector signs in through your browser on first use.

faq.question: When does a paid search start?
faq.answer: Paid work starts after you approve the exact maximum in the quote. Drafting the search specification does not start paid work.

faq.question: What information goes to SpecStream?
faq.answer: The compile step sends your search request to SpecStream before you approve a price. Leave out passwords and confidential details.

faq.question: Does the table include every match on the web?
faq.answer: The table shows the rows the service returns. Retrieving every results page does not guarantee that the search found every match on the web.

faq.question: Can I verify why a row matched?
faq.answer: Yes. You can review condition checks and their sources. Returned values also include source URLs.

faq.question: Can I download the results?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for a file export of the returned rows.
